standard_prerequisites.name: Finite generation of Ext^i_A(K, M) for pseudo-coherent K and finite M
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the power-torsion hypothesis effective, giving the annihilator I^t.

standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of the image of Ext^i_A(K, I^nM) -> Ext^i_A(K, M) for large n
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the annihilation input that the long exact sequence consumes on both sides.

standard_prerequisites.name: The long exact sequence of Ext attached to a short exact sequence of modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the four-term sequence from which essential constancy is deduced.

core_obligations: For a finite A-module M, use pseudo-coherence of K to conclude that Ext^i_A(K, M) is a finite A-module, hence for i >= a annihilated by I^t for some t >= 0 (proof lines 29796-29798).
Use the induced-topology lemma to conclude that the image of Ext^i_A(K, I^nM) -> Ext^i_A(K, M) is zero for some n > 0 (proof lines 29799-29801).

Apply the long exact sequence of Ext to the short exact sequence 0 -> I^nM -> M -> M/I^nM -> 0 to obtain the displayed four-term exact sequence relating Ext^i_A(K, I^nM), Ext^i_A(K, M), Ext^i_A(K, M/I^nM) and Ext^{i+1}_A(K, I^nM) (proof lines 29802-29807).

Apply the vanishing of the first paragraph to the finite A-modules I^m M to conclude that the systems Ext^i_A(K, I^nM) and Ext^{i+1}_A(K, I^nM) are essentially constant with value 0 (proof lines 29808-29810).
Conclude by a diagram chase that the system Ext^i_A(K, M/I^nM) is essentially constant with value Ext^i_A(K, M), which is the statement (proof lines 29810-29812).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian ring A, an ideal I, a pseudo-coherent object K of D(A), and an integer a, and assumes that for every finite A-module M the modules Ext^i_A(K, M) are I-power torsion for i >= a; it concludes that for i >= a and M finite the system Ext^i_A(K, M/I^nM) is essentially constant with value Ext^i_A(K, M) = lim Ext^i_A(K, M/I^nM) (source lines 29781-29793). The proof begins with finite generation: since K is pseudo-coherent, each Ext^i_A(K, M) is a finite A-module, so for i >= a it is annihilated by I^t for some t >= 0 (proof lines 29796-29798). The substantive step is a vanishing of images: the induced-topology lemma shows that the image of Ext^i_A(K, I^nM) -> Ext^i_A(K, M) is zero for some n > 0 (proof lines 29799-29801). The proof then applies the long exact sequence of Ext to the short exact sequence 0 -> I^nM -> M -> M/I^nM -> 0, obtaining the displayed four-term exact sequence Ext^i_A(K, I^nM) -> Ext^i_A(K, M) -> Ext^i_A(K, M/I^nM) -> Ext^{i+1}_A(K, I^nM) (proof lines 29802-29807). Since the systems Ext^i_A(K, I^nM) and Ext^{i+1}_A(K, I^nM) are essentially constant with value 0 by the preceding vanishing applied to the finite modules I^m M, a diagram chase completes the proof (proof lines 29808-29812). The non-routine content is the systematic use of the long exact sequence with a two-sided vanishing to force the middle system to be essentially constant.
